sections.overview: The Eurasian Whimbrel is a migratory curlew that breeds across northern regions and winters mainly in warmer coastal areas.
sections.identification: It is smaller than the Eurasian Curlew (Numenius arquata), with a shorter bill and a pale central crown stripe bordered by dark stripes; it is much smaller than the Far Eastern Curlew (N. madagascariensis).
sections.habitat: It breeds on northern moorland, tundra and open boggy ground, and uses coasts, estuaries and sometimes inland wetlands during migration and winter.
sections.diet: Its food varies by season: it takes insects and molluscs on breeding grounds, and also feeds on crabs, shrimps, worms and molluscs during passage.
sections.behavior: Many birds pass through Europe in spring and autumn between northern breeding areas and African or southern Asian wintering grounds.
sections.reproduction: It nests on the ground in open northern habitats, often in a shallow scrape among vegetation.
sections.ecology: The Eurasian Whimbrel shares its genus with the larger Eurasian and Far Eastern curlews and the tiny Little Curlew; their profiles compare their sizes, bills and ranges. Its closest relative is the Bristle-thighed Curlew (Numenius tahitiensis), whose Pacific island migration contrasts with the Whimbrel’s broad Afro-Eurasian routes; see that profile for the reciprocal comparison.
sections.conservation: BirdLife lists the species as Least Concern globally.
